title: Pre-shot actions
lead: Which actions and chains of actions precede better chances, how they change the defense's shape, and how spacing relates to outcomes.

blocks.text: Which actions, and which orders of actions, come before the best chances?

items: Each half-court chance becomes the list of its actions, in the order they happened, up to the shot
Actions are SkillCorner's picks, handoffs, off-ball screens, drives, isolations, post-ups and closeouts, plus the site's basket cuts, pick-and-pops and paint touches
Outcomes are the chance's points, shot quality (xPts per FGA), turnovers, free-throw trips and offensive rebounds on live misses
Actions are SkillCorner's detections plus the site's cuts and pops. Both miss some actions and mislabel others
A long chain is also a long chance, and the shot clock forces shots late in long chains, so counts and orders are confounded with time

blocks.text: At the release of the shot (FGA chances), how many attackers were beyond the arc and how many defenders were in the key, against the shot's quality.

items: Spacing at release is tied to where the shot is. A layup puts the shooter and his defender in the key
The chance-average view is less tied to the shot spot but still reflects the opponent and the lineup

sections.title: What this shows and does not

items: It shows which actions and short sequences come before better and worse chances, and how each action moves the defense in the next two seconds
It does not separate the action from who runs it, against whom, or how much time was left
Model the chance outcome on the last action, with team and opponent terms
Use the shape changes (hull, key, room off the ball) as the mechanism
Test whether an action that shrinks the defense more leads to a better next shot
